3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that the suit land measuring 301 decimals appertaining to Plot No. 21 in C.S. Khatian No. 1234 of Mouza Arasthita 305 under Police Station Roypura (old) at present Shibpur Police Station, District Narsingdi described in the schedule of the plaint belonged to Shaheb Ali, Zafar Ali and Felan in equal share and their names were correctly recorded in C.S. Khatian. Zafar Ali got 1-1⁄3 share, i.e. 100 decimals of land of disputed plot in the northern side. While Zafar Ali was in possession he died leaving behind 3(three) sons, namely Zinnat Ali, Sorat Ali and Minnat Ali. Sorat Ali while in possession sold 0.7 decimals of land mentioning the specific boundary to Azimuddin by registered deed No. 3549 dated 16.11.1963 and handed over possession. While said Azimuddin was in possession over 25(twenty-five) years by way of a registered deed of exchange No. 7989 dated 04.12.1988 relinquished 0.7 decimals of land in favour of Ibrahim Sarkar and handed over possession. While he was in possession of the suit land he executed and registered deed of exchange No. 9722 dated 07.12.1990 in favour of plaintiff and handed over the possession and since then the plaintiff has been possessing and enjoying the suit land by splitting up jama in his own name without any let or hindrance from any quarter. It has further been stated that the plaintiff filled up low land by earth and also constructed pucca wall for constructing building over the suit land within the knowledge of the people of that locality. While the construction was going on the greedy defendant threatened to dispossess the plaintiff from the suit land with the help of arms and ammunition and hence the suit. 

 5. The defendants contested the suit by filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint and contended, inter alia, that the plaintiff has got no prima-facie case and he has possession over the suit property. Shaheb Ali, Zafar Ali, and Felan were the owners of total 301 decimals of land along with 3(three) others plots in Arali Mouza bearing No. 305 of the settlement survey. The names of the said owners were duly recorded and published in C.S. Khatian No. 1234. Among the above mentioned 3(three) brothers, Zafar Ali obtained his 1/3 share in total lands measuring 300 decimals a segment cut out from the northern portion of total 230 decimals of suit plot No. 21. The said Zafar Ali while remaining in possession having right, title and interest over the said property, died leaving behind his 3(three) sons Jinnat Ali, Sorat Ali and Minnat Ali as his heirs. S.A. Khatian No. 1275 and R.S. Khatian No. 739 were rightly prepared and published in the names of said Minnat Ali's 3(three) sons and other co-sharers. Among the later mentioned 3(three) brothers, Sorat Ali got 34 decimals of northern portion of the suit plot and while he was in possession, he transferred 7(seven) decimals of land in the western part out of 34 decimals of land in his possession to Azimuddin, the father of 34 decimals of land in his possession to Azimuddin, the father of the plaintiff by a kabala dated 16.11.1963 which was later acquired by the Government of Dhaka Monohardi C& B Road, by L.A. Case No. 90/66-67. Minnat Ali got 33 decimals of land in the farthest eastern portion and transferred 3½ decimals of land in favour of Azimuddin by the kabala dated 30.11.1984 and handed over possession to him. Later Azimuddin transferred the said 31⁄2decimals of land to one Ibrahim Sarkar by deed of Ewaz (mutual exchange deed) and handed over possession. Minnat Ali and Sorat Ali, together sold out 14 decimals of land to Afsaruddin and others by kabala dated 17.07.1983 and also handed over possession to them. Afsaruddin while remaining in ownership and possession transferred 3½ decimals of land to Abul Basher by kabala dated 18,08.1983 and subsequently Abul Basher sold 3½ decimals of land to the defendants by kabala No. 5706 dated 18.09.1985 and also handed over possession to them. The defendants were trying to build homestead in it encircling by a wall of 3(three) feet high and carrying out necessary earth filling works. The defendants denied that the plaintiff has right, title, interest and possession over the suit land and they prayed that the suit be dismissed.
